unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Her smile and 'real proud' still imply acceptance.

The girl smiled. “I’ll go through with it all right. And I’m real proud to be chosen!
The girl smiled. “I’m real proud to be chosen! What am I to do with them afterwards?”

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft cut 'Then be ready--I'm going to say good-bye.' The revision then changed 'in a louder tone' to 'loudly' and dropped 'in his'. The contrast with his earlier lowered voice, and the signal that the farewell is a staged hand-off, both weaken.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'He lowered his voice' (rev p9) still sets up some contrast, and the palm-to-palm packet line follows immediately.

evidence.quote: “Then be ready--I’m going to say good-bye.” He took her hand in his.
He took her hand in his. “Good-bye. Good luck to you,” he said in a louder tone.
He took her hand. “Good-bye. Good luck to you,” he said loudly.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore 'Then be ready--I’m going to say good-bye.' and 'in a louder tone' (about 8 words).
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required essential ('goodbye loudly as cover'); partly a planning gap, since the 'be ready' line is not protected.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The plan's 'says goodbye loudly as cover' becomes inference only. Readers may take the farewell as sentiment rather than misdirection.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Good-bye's function as cover weakened
